messages:
maria (People Ops): Quick Q — our 401(k) auto-escalation schedule is set to bump deferral by 1% annually. An employee is going on unpaid parental leave next month and asked if escalation will still apply or if we can pause it. Anyone handled this with Principal/ADP/Gusto?

jamal (Payroll): Short answer: it depends. For unpaid leave there are no payroll deductions, so no money is taken. Whether the election % still advances depends on who runs the escalation (vendor vs payroll) and whether we have a suspend flag.

alex (IC): I'm the employee — going on unpaid leave 2026-04-01. I don't want my deferral to increase while I'm off. What's the simplest way to pause?

liz (Benefits): Plan doc allows auto-escalation but vendor-driven. Some vendors (Principal, Fidelity) support suspending escalation per participant; others require a plan admin change. Also note: catch-up (50+) is separate and generally needs manual enrollment.

maria (People Ops): Vendor is Principal for our 401(k). @jamal can you check Principal's process? Also we should confirm how this interacts with company match.

jamal (Payroll): Opening ticket with Principal now. In ADP/Gusto the payroll file accepts an `escalation_suspended` flag if vendor sends it. If not, we might need to submit a signed form to Principal to stop future election changes. For unpaid pay periods, payroll won't deduct anything even if election changes are queued.

gusto-bot: New support ticket created: #PRINC-4123 — "Auto-escalation pause request + parental leave". ETA: 3 business days.

liz (Benefits): Action items: 1) Confirm whether Principal sends election updates with an effective date or per payroll period. 2) Confirm whether the employee portal will show the upcoming auto-escalation while on leave. 3) Draft a short template for employees to request pause/resume. I'll draft it below.

alex (IC): Important: include steps for resuming the escalation on return and whether the escalation cycle picks up where it left off or restarts.

maria (People Ops): Please draft the template and I can own the comms. Also remind managers not to change elections locally without consulting Benefits. Match is based on actual contributions — if no deductions, no match.

liz (Benefits): Draft template: 

```
Subject: Request to pause 401(k) auto-escalation during unpaid leave

Hi Benefits team,

I will be on unpaid parental leave from 2026-04-01 to 2026-06-30. Please pause my 401(k) auto-escalation effective my leave start date. My employee ID: 12345.

- I understand contributions won't be taken while unpaid.
- Please confirm if this affects my scheduled match or catch-up elections.
- Please confirm the steps needed to resume escalation on my return.

Thanks,
Alex
```

jamal (Payroll): Principal responded to #PRINC-4123: they can suspend auto-escalation for individual participants, but it requires a signed participant form (e-sign acceptable). They will also include an `escalation_suspended` flag in the next export once processed. Attaching form to the ticket.

maria (People Ops): Perfect. @alex we'll need you to sign that form. @jamal can you paste the form link once attached? I'll coordinate sending it and confirming return/resume dates.

jamal (Payroll): Form attached to ticket: https://principal.example.com/forms/escalation_suspend.pdf (internal). Ticket update: once signature received, Principal will process within 2 payroll cycles and include the `escalation_suspended` flag in the vendor feed.

alex (IC): Got it — I'll sign today. Does this affect year-end deferral totals or taxes? Trying to understand taxable reporting if contributions stop mid-year.

liz (Benefits): Stopping escalation doesn't change prior contributions. For tax reporting (W-2/401k deferrals) you'll simply have lower pre-tax deferrals for the months on unpaid leave. No immediate taxable event for pausing. If you want to catch up after return, we can discuss bumping the deferral or contributing catch-up (if eligible).

maria (People Ops): (typo fix) — Liz, can we add an FAQ snippet to handbook: "Auto-escalation applies only when contributions are being deducted; for unpaid leave contact Benefits to pause/resume." I'll add that after you confirm wording.

liz (Benefits): Yes — suggested FAQ: "If you go on unpaid leave, auto-escalation does not increase your actual contributions unless payroll deductions occur. Contact Benefits to suspend auto-escalation while on unpaid leave; we will resume it on request or on your return date."

jamal (Payroll): Ticket #PRINC-4123 status: awaiting signed participant form. ETA to close: 2 business days after signature. I'll update here when processed and when the flag appears in the export.

gusto-bot: Ticket #PRINC-4123 updated by jamal — status: awaiting signature.

alex (IC): Thanks everyone — signing now. Appreciate the clear steps :thumbsup:

maria (People Ops): Thanks all — when jamal posts the processed confirmation I'll add the handbook blurb and post a short how-to in #benefits-updates.
